711	**Key patterns:**
712	- `isactr:ConnectorActivity` is the generic IS activity type (`xmlns:isactr="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/integration-service-activities/isactr"`)
713	- `Configuration` holds a base64-encoded GZip-compressed blob — **never construct this manually**, it comes from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`
714	- `ConnectionId` is the Integration Service connection GUID
715	- `UiPathActivityTypeId` identifies the specific connector operation
716	- `FieldObjects` define input/output fields with `isactr:FieldObject` elements
717	- Output types reference a JIT-generated assembly (e.g., `CDF573A04A6_search_r.VeKd1XI2qK1X56UO2Br3Ui3`)
718	- The generated assembly name and namespace imports are connector-specific — always use `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output
719	
720	## Property Binding: Attributes vs Child Elements
721	
722	XAML properties can be set in two ways: as XML attributes or as child elements. Both are valid XAML, but some properties only work reliably in one form.
723	
724	### Attribute Syntax (Inline)
725	```xml
726	<ui:LogMessage Message="[myVar]" Level="Info" />
727	```
728	
729	### Child Element Syntax (Property Element)
730	```xml
731	<ui:SomeActivity>
732	  <ui:SomeActivity.Result>
733	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">[outputVar]</OutArgument>
734	  </ui:SomeActivity.Result>
735	</ui:SomeActivity>
736	```
737	
738	### When to Use Which
739	
740	**Simple values** (strings, enums, booleans, VB expressions in brackets) almost always work as attributes:
741	```xml
742	DisplayName="My Activity" Message="[variable]" Level="Info"
743	```
744	
745	**Output properties** (`OutArgument`, `Result`) may require child element syntax. Some activities accept `Result="[var]"` as an attribute; others only work with the expanded child element form. If an attribute-form output binding causes a validation error, try the child element form.
746	
747	**Complex objects** (BackupSlot, MailboxArgument, ActivityAction, dictionaries) always require child element syntax — they cannot be expressed as a single attribute value.
748	
749	**Strings containing literal `[` or `]`** (e.g., UIA special-key tokens like `[k(enter)]`, `[d(ctrl)]`, `[u(ctrl)]`) require child element syntax. The attribute form `Foo="["…[k(enter)]"]"` runs correctly because the runtime VB compiler reads quoted string literals correctly, but the literal brackets inside the string collide with the outer `[ … ]` VB expression markers and the value will not render in Studio. See [common-pitfalls.md § NTypeInto `Text` with literal `[k(...)]` special-key tokens](common-pitfalls.md#ntypeinto-text-with-literal-k-special-key-tokens).
750	
751	### Version-Sensitive Properties
752	
753	Properties may exist in one package version but not another. If `validate` reports "Could not find member 'PropertyName'":
754	1. The property may not exist in the installed package version — remove it
755	2. The property may have been renamed between versions — check examples from the same package version
756	3. Use `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output as the authoritative set of properties for the installed version
757	
758	## ConnectorActivity Internals
759	
760	Understanding the structure of `isactr:ConnectorActivity` so you know what you can and cannot edit.
761	
762	### Properties (What They Are)
763	
764	| Property | Editable? | Description |
765	|----------|-----------|-------------|
766	| `Configuration` | **NEVER** | ZIP-compressed, Base64-encoded JSON blob containing the full activity schema (fields, types, connector metadata). This is obtained and computed for you using the `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` command. Do not parse, modify, or construct manually. |
767	| `ConnectionId` | Yes (replace GUID) | Integration Service connection GUID. Use `uip is connections list [connector-key]` to discover available connections and their IDs. |
768	| `UiPathActivityTypeId` | **NEVER** | Identifies the specific connector operation. Obtain using `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` or `uip rpa activities find`. |
769	| `DisplayName` | Yes | Human-readable activity name for the designer. |
770	
771	### FieldObjects (Input/Output Interface)
772	
773	`FieldObjects` is the collection of input and output fields. Each `isactr:FieldObject` has:
774	
775	| Attribute | Description |
776	|-----------|-------------|
777	| `Name` | Field identifier (maps to the connector API parameter). Must match exactly what `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` returns. |
778	| `Type` | One of: `FieldArgument` (contains an Activity Argument), `FieldLiteral` (contains a literal value), `FilterTreeValue` (filter builder criteria), `None` (empty). |
779	
780	**What you CAN edit in FieldObjects:**
781	- **Input field values**: Change the `InArgument` value inside a `FieldObject.Value` to set different input data (e.g., change a search query string).
782	- **Bind to variables**: Replace a literal value with a variable reference using `<CSharpValue>` (e.g., `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:String">myVariable</CSharpValue>`).
783	
784	**What you CANNOT edit:**
785	- Field `Name` values — these must match the connector API schema exactly.
786	- Field `Type` values — these are determined by the connector metadata.
787	- Output field structure — the `OutArgument` types reference JIT-generated assemblies.
788	- Adding/removing FieldObjects — the set of fields comes from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`.
789	
790	### JIT-Generated Assemblies
791	
792	Output fields often use types from JIT-compiled assemblies with hashed names:
793	```
794	CDF573A04A6_search_r.VeKd1XI2qK1X56UO2Br3Ui3
795	^connection(last10)   ^operation   ^content hash
796	```
797	
798	These assembly names are:
799	- **Unpredictable** — derived from SHA-512 hashes of the type schema
800	- **Connection-specific** — different connections produce different hashes
801	- **Generated by the runtime** — you cannot create or reference them without `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`
802	
803	The corresponding namespace imports and assembly references MUST come from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output. Never construct them.
804	
805	### What `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` Returns for Dynamic Activities
806	
807	When you call `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` with `isDynamicActivity: true`, it returns everything needed:
808	1. The complete `<isactr:ConnectorActivity>` XAML element with `Configuration` blob, `UiPathActivityTypeId`, and `FieldObjects`
809	2. All required `xmlns` declarations for the root `<Activity>` element
810	3. All required namespace imports and references
811	
812	Use this output as-is. The only things you should modify are:
813	- `DisplayName` — set a meaningful name
814	- `ConnectionId` — if swapping to a different connection of the same connector type
815	- Input `FieldObject` values — to set the actual data for your workflow
816

1	# Common Activity Card
2	
3	**Package anchor:** `UiPath.System.Activities` 26.4 (verified against 26.4.1-preview).
4	
5	Copy-safe snippets for the 13 activities listed below. **Supersedes the Rule 21 discovery procedure for these activities only** — when authoring one of these, skip `activities find`, skip `activities get-default-xaml`, skip the per-activity `<Activity>.md` read, and copy the snippet here.
6	
7	For every other activity, full Rule 21 applies. Self-extending this card by personal judgment ("this one feels simple, I'll skip the procedure") is the failure mode.
8	
9	## Card entries
10	
11	`Sequence` · `If` · `Switch<T>` · `TryCatch` · `While` · `DoWhile` · `ForEach<T>` · `Assign` · `LogMessage` · `WriteLine` · `Delay` · `Throw` · `Rethrow`
12	
13	## How to read the snippets
14	
15	Snippets below are **fragments** intended to drop inside a complete `<Activity>` root. The root must declare:
16	
17	```xml
18	xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
19	xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
20	xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"
21	```
22	
23	Entries that need additional prefixes (`xmlns:s` for `System` types, `xmlns:sc` for `System.Collections`) call them out in the "XAML prefix" line. For modern Windows-target projects use `assembly=System.Private.CoreLib`; for Legacy (.NET 4.6.1) projects use `assembly=mscorlib`.
24	
25	Snippets use the property-element form with `<VisualBasicValue>` / `<VisualBasicReference>`. For C# expression projects, apply [xaml/csharp-activity-binding-guide.md](xaml/csharp-activity-binding-guide.md).
26

29	## Group A — Control flow
30	
31	### Sequence
32	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Sequence`
33	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace (`xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"`); no `ui:` prefix.
34	
35	**Snippet:**
36	```xml
37	<Sequence DisplayName="Sequence">
38	  <!-- child activities in execution order -->
39	</Sequence>
40	```
41	
42	**Notes:** `Sequence` is the canonical container wrap required by Rule 24 in every body/branch slot of `If`, `Switch`, `TryCatch`, `While`, `DoWhile`, `ForEach`, `Pick`, etc. — even with a single child. Declare `<Sequence.Variables>` only when this sequence owns local variables. ViewState is **optional** for Sequences (Rule 20); required only when the parent is `Flowchart`, `StateMachine`, or `ProcessDiagram`.
43	
44	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Sequence.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Sequence.md)

48	### If
49	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.If`
50	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
51	
52	**Snippet:**
53	```xml
54	<If DisplayName="If">
55	  <If.Condition>
56	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">
57	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="counter < 10" />
58	    </InArgument>
59	  </If.Condition>
60	  <If.Then>
61	    <Sequence DisplayName="Then">
62	      <!-- then branch -->
63	    </Sequence>
64	  </If.Then>
65	  <If.Else>
66	    <Sequence DisplayName="Else">
67	      <!-- else branch -->
68	    </Sequence>
69	  </If.Else>
70	</If>
71	```
72	
73	**Notes:** Both `If.Then` and `If.Else` slots must wrap their body in `<Sequence>` per Rule 24. Omit `<If.Else>` entirely when no else branch is needed — do not emit an empty `<If.Else></If.Else>`. For multi-branch `else if … else if`, use `IfElseIfV2` (off this card; see `ElseIf.md`).
74	
75	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/If.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/If.md)

79	### Switch<T>
80	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Switch`1`
81	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
82	
83	**Snippet** (typed `Int32` example — change `x:TypeArguments` for other types):
84	```xml
85	<Switch x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Switch">
86	  <Switch.Expression>
87	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
88	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="status" />
89	    </InArgument>
90	  </Switch.Expression>
91	  <Sequence x:Key="1" DisplayName="Case 1">
92	    <!-- case body for status == 1 -->
93	  </Sequence>
94	  <Sequence x:Key="2" DisplayName="Case 2">
95	    <!-- case body for status == 2 -->
96	  </Sequence>
97	  <Switch.Default>
98	    <Sequence DisplayName="Default">
99	      <!-- fallback body -->
100	    </Sequence>
101	  </Switch.Default>
102	</Switch>
103	```
104	
105	**Notes:** Each case body and `Switch.Default` must wrap their content in `<Sequence>` per Rule 24. Case keys are declared via `x:Key="<literal>"` on each case-body child directly inside `<Switch>` — the `Cases` dictionary is not declared explicitly. For string keys: `x:TypeArguments="x:String"` and `x:Key="someString"`.
106	
107	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Switch.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Switch.md)

111	### TryCatch
112	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.TryCatch`
113	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; also declare `xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the exception type (Legacy/.NET 4.6.1 projects use `assembly=mscorlib`).
114	
115	**Snippet:**
116	```xml
117	<TryCatch DisplayName="Try Catch">
118	  <TryCatch.Try>
119	    <Sequence DisplayName="Try">
120	      <!-- guarded body -->
121	    </Sequence>
122	  </TryCatch.Try>
123	  <TryCatch.Catches>
124	    <Catch x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
125	      <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
126	        <ActivityAction.Argument>
127	          <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" Name="exception" />
128	        </ActivityAction.Argument>
129	        <Sequence DisplayName="Catch">
130	          <!-- handler body; reference iterator variable "exception" -->
131	        </Sequence>
132	      </ActivityAction>
133	    </Catch>
134	  </TryCatch.Catches>
135	  <TryCatch.Finally>
136	    <Sequence DisplayName="Finally">
137	      <!-- finally body -->
138	    </Sequence>
139	  </TryCatch.Finally>
140	</TryCatch>
141	```
142	
143	**Notes:** `Try`, every `Catch.Action`, and `Finally` must wrap their body in `<Sequence>` per Rule 24. Each `Catch` requires its own `<ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="...">` holding a `<DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="..." Name="exception" />` — the `Name` is the variable name the handler body uses. Place specific exception types before `s:Exception`. Omit `<TryCatch.Finally>` entirely when not needed. For strategy — exception taxonomy, Retry Scope, ContinueOnError, screenshot-on-error, Global Exception Handler — see [error-handling-guide.md](error-handling-guide.md).
144	
145	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/TryCatch.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/TryCatch.md)

149	### While
150	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.InterruptibleWhile` (Studio emits **this**, not the framework `System.Activities.Statements.While`)
151	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`.
152	
153	**Snippet:**
154	```xml
155	<ui:InterruptibleWhile DisplayName="While">
156	  <ui:InterruptibleWhile.Condition>
157	    <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="counter < 10" />
158	  </ui:InterruptibleWhile.Condition>
159	  <ui:InterruptibleWhile.Body>
160	    <Sequence DisplayName="Body">
161	      <!-- iteration body -->
162	    </Sequence>
163	  </ui:InterruptibleWhile.Body>
164	</ui:InterruptibleWhile>
165	```
166	
167	**Non-obvious properties:**
168	- `MaxIterations` — `InArgument<int>` — upper bound; `0` means **unlimited**. Default `0`. Set to a positive value to guard against infinite loops.
169	- `CurrentIndex` — `OutArgument<int>` — zero-based iteration counter; bind to a variable when the body needs the index.
170	
171	**Notes:** Studio uses `InterruptibleWhile`, not the framework `While`. The body must be `<Sequence>`-wrapped per Rule 24. `Condition` is evaluated **before** each iteration; if false on entry, the body never runs.
172	
173	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/While.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/While.md)
174	
175	---
176	
177	### Do While
178	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.InterruptibleDoWhile` (Studio emits **this**, not the framework `System.Activities.Statements.DoWhile`)
179	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`.
180	
181	**Snippet:**
182	```xml
183	<ui:InterruptibleDoWhile DisplayName="Do While">
184	  <ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Body>
185	    <Sequence DisplayName="Body">
186	      <!-- iteration body -->
187	    </Sequence>
188	  </ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Body>
189	  <ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Condition>
190	    <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="counter < 10" />
191	  </ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Condition>
192	</ui:InterruptibleDoWhile>
193	```
194	
195	**Non-obvious properties:**
196	- `MaxIterations` — `InArgument<int>` — upper bound; `0` means **unlimited**. Default `0`.
197	- `CurrentIndex` — `OutArgument<int>` — zero-based iteration counter.
198	
199	**Notes:** Studio uses `InterruptibleDoWhile`, not the framework `DoWhile`. The body must be `<Sequence>`-wrapped per Rule 24. Body executes **at least once**; `Condition` is evaluated **after** each iteration.
200	
201	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/DoWhile.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/DoWhile.md)
202	
203	---
204	
205	### For Each<T>
206	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.ForEach`1` (Studio emits **this**, not the framework `System.Activities.Statements.ForEach<T>`)
207	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`; declare `xmlns:sc="clr-namespace:System.Collections;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the (non-generic) `IEnumerable` argument typing.
208	
209	**Snippet** (typed `String` example — change `x:TypeArguments` on the outer activity and on the inner `ActivityAction`/`DelegateInArgument` to match the element type):
210	```xml
211	<ui:ForEach x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="For Each">
212	  <ui:ForEach.Values>
213	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="sc:IEnumerable">
214	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="sc:IEnumerable" ExpressionText="myList" />
215	    </InArgument>
216	  </ui:ForEach.Values>
217	  <ui:ForEach.Body>
218	    <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="x:String">
219	      <ActivityAction.Argument>
220	        <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="item" />
221	      </ActivityAction.Argument>
222	      <Sequence DisplayName="Body">
223	        <!-- iteration body; reference iterator variable "item" -->
224	      </Sequence>
225	    </ActivityAction>
226	  </ui:ForEach.Body>
227	</ui:ForEach>
228	```
229	
230	**Non-obvious properties:**
231	- `Values` — `InArgument<System.Collections.IEnumerable>` — **non-generic** `IEnumerable`, not `IEnumerable<T>` (verified against `ForEachBase<T>.Values`). The element type `T` comes from the outer `x:TypeArguments` on `<ui:ForEach>`, not from `Values`.
232	- `Body` — `ActivityAction<T>` — must be set via the `<ui:ForEach.Body>` property element (it is NOT the ContentProperty; placing a bare `<ActivityAction>` directly inside `<ui:ForEach>` produces `Cannot set unknown member '...Implementation'`).
233	- `MaxIterations` — `InArgument<int>` — upper bound; `0` means **unlimited**. Default `0`.
234	- `CurrentIndex` — `OutArgument<int>` — zero-based iteration counter.
235	
236	**Notes:** Studio uses `UiPath.Core.Activities.ForEach`, not the framework `ForEach<T>`. The iterator variable name (`item` in the snippet) is set via `DelegateInArgument.Name` on the inner `ActivityAction.Argument` — auto-suggested by Studio based on element type. Body must be `<Sequence>`-wrapped per Rule 24.
237	
238	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/ForEach.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/ForEach.md)
239	
240	---
241	
242	## Group B — Data + logging
243	
244	### Assign
245	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Assign`1` (generic; preferred) — non-generic `Assign` only when both sides are `object`.
246	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
247	
248	**Snippet** (typed `Int32` example):
249	```xml
250	<Assign x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Assign">
251	  <Assign.To>
252	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
253	      <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="counter" />
254	    </OutArgument>
255	  </Assign.To>
256	  <Assign.Value>
257	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
258	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="counter + 1" />
259	    </InArgument>
260	  </Assign.Value>
261	</Assign>
262	```
263	
264	**Notes:** Prefer the generic `Assign<T>` form — typed args surface mismatch errors at `validate` time. `To` must be a writable expression (variable, argument, indexer) — Studio's emitter uses `VisualBasicReference` (or `CSharpReference` in C# projects) for the writable side and `VisualBasicValue` (or `CSharpValue`) for the readable side. One `Assign` per target — no multi-target form.
265	
266	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Assign.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Assign.md)
267	
268	---
269	
270	### Log Message
271	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.LogMessage`
272	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`; no extra prefix needed (`x:Object` uses the root `xmlns:x`).
273	
274	**Snippet:**
275	```xml
276	<ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log Message">
277	  <ui:LogMessage.Message>
278	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
279	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="$"Processed {count} items"" />
280	    </InArgument>
281	  </ui:LogMessage.Message>
282	</ui:LogMessage>
283	```
284	
285	**Non-obvious properties:**
286	- `Level` — `InArgument<LogLevel>` — required-in-practice; **default `Info`** but the skip-tax hides it from `get-default-xaml`. Enum values: `Trace` | `Info` | `Warn` | `Error` | `Fatal`.
287	- `Message` — `InArgument<object>` — **not** `string`. Accepts any expression; the activity calls `.ToString()`. In VB projects, bracket shorthand can hold composite expressions such as `[$"x = {x}"]`; in C# projects, use `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object">...</CSharpValue>`.
288	
289	**Notes:** Prefer `LogMessage` over `WriteLine` for any output that must appear in Orchestrator. `Level` defaults to `Info`; omit only when you want `Info` and the explicit attribute clutters the snippet.
290	
291	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/LogMessage.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/LogMessage.md)
292	
293	---
294	
295	### Write Line
296	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.WriteLine`
297	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
298	
299	**Snippet:**
300	```xml
301	<WriteLine DisplayName="Write Line">
302	  <WriteLine.Text>
303	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
304	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="$"processed {count} items"" />
305	    </InArgument>
306	  </WriteLine.Text>
307	</WriteLine>
308	```
309	
310	**Notes:** Writes to stdout only — invisible in Orchestrator. Prefer `LogMessage` whenever Orchestrator visibility matters. Do **not** set `TextWriter` — its default (`Console.Out`) is correct for every Studio and `uip rpa run` context.
311	
312	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/WriteLine.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/WriteLine.md)
313	
314	---
315	
316	### Delay
317	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Delay`
318	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; declare `xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the `TimeSpan` argument type (Legacy/.NET 4.6.1 projects use `assembly=mscorlib`).
319	
320	**Snippet:**
321	```xml
322	<Delay DisplayName="Delay">
323	  <Delay.Duration>
324	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="s:TimeSpan">
325	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="s:TimeSpan" ExpressionText="TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)" />
326	    </InArgument>
327	  </Delay.Duration>
328	</Delay>
329	```
330	
331	**Notes:** `Duration` must produce a `TimeSpan`. In VB projects, bracket shorthand such as `[TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)]` is valid; in C# projects, use `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="s:TimeSpan">TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)</CSharpValue>` or a literal attribute such as `Duration="00:00:05"`. Blocks the workflow thread for the full duration — avoid inside `ForEach`/`While` bodies where it multiplies. Do **not** use `Delay` to wait on external state; use `RetryScope`, `WaitForElement`, or a polling loop with a `Condition` instead.
332	
333	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Delay.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Delay.md)
334	
335	---
336	
337	### Throw
338	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Throw`
339	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; also declare `xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the exception argument type (Legacy/.NET 4.6.1 projects use `assembly=mscorlib`).
340	
341	**Snippet:**
342	```xml
343	<Throw DisplayName="Throw">
344	  <Throw.Exception>
345	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
346	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" ExpressionText="new InvalidOperationException("Invoice total is negative")" />
347	    </InArgument>
348	  </Throw.Exception>
349	</Throw>
350	```
351	
352	**Notes:** `Exception` is a **constructor expression**, not a string. `Throw.Exception = "message"` is invalid. Use a domain-specific exception type (e.g., `BusinessRuleException`) when downstream `Catch` handlers need to distinguish business errors from system errors. Use `Rethrow` (inside a `Catch` body) to preserve the original stack trace instead.
353	
354	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Throw.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Throw.md)
355	
356	---
357	
358	### Rethrow
359	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Rethrow`
360	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
361	
362	**Snippet:**
363	```xml
364	<Rethrow DisplayName="Rethrow" />
365	```
366	
367	**Notes:** Zero properties. **Only valid inside a `Catch.Action` body** — using it outside a `Catch` is a runtime `InvalidOperationException`. Preserves the original exception's stack trace; use `Throw new <Type>(...)` instead when you want to translate to a different exception type. Place `Rethrow` last in the `Catch` body — anything after it is unreachable.
368	
369	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Rethrow.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Rethrow.md)
370	
371	---
372

parameters.content:
<Activity mc:Ignorable="sap sap2010" x:Class="Main" mva:VisualBasic.Settings="{x:Null}"
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
  xmlns:isactr="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/integration-service-activities/isactr"
  xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
  xmlns:mva="clr-namespace:Microsoft.VisualBasic.Activities;assembly=System.Activities"
  xmlns:sap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities/presentation"
  xmlns:sap2010="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2010/xaml/activities/presentation"
  xmlns:sco="clr-namespace:System.Collections.ObjectModel;assembly=mscorlib"
  xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"
  xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml">

  <x:Members>
    <!-- The Slack Channel ID to look up (e.g. "C12345678").
         Find it in Slack: right-click the channel → View channel details → Copy channel ID (bottom of "About" tab). -->
    <x:Property Name="in_ChannelId" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
  </x:Members>

  <TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="x:String">
      <x:String>System.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Statements</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Expressions</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.Validation</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Activities.XamlIntegration</x:String>
      <x:String>Microsoft.VisualBasic</x:String>
      <x:String>Microsoft.VisualBasic.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>System</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections.Generic</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Collections.ObjectModel</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Data</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Diagnostics</x:String>
      <x:String>System.IO</x:String>
      <x:String>System.Linq</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Core</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.Core.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.IntegrationService.Activities.Runtime.Activities</x:String>
      <x:String>UiPath.IntegrationService.Activities.Runtime.Models</x:String>
    </sco:Collection>
  </TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>

  <TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>
    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="AssemblyReference">
      <AssemblyReference>System.Activities</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>Microsoft.VisualBasic</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Private.CoreLib</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>mscorlib</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Linq</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Data</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Data.Common</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>System.Core</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>UiPath.System.Activities</AssemblyReference>
      <AssemblyReference>UiPath.IntegrationService.Activities.Runtime</AssemblyReference>
    </sco:Collection>
  </TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>

  <Sequence DisplayName="Get Slack Channel Description" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="Sequence_1">
    <Sequence.Variables>
      <!-- Holds the raw channel record returned by the ConnectorActivity -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:Object" Name="channelInfo" />
      <!-- Extracted from channelInfo at runtime via VB late-binding -->
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="channelName" Default="" />
      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="channelDescription" Default="" />
    </Sequence.Variables>

    <!-- ── Step 1: Log that we are starting ── -->
    <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log: Starting lookup" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="LogMessage_1">
      <ui:LogMessage.Message>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object"
            ExpressionText="$"[SlackChannelDescription] Fetching info for channel ID: {in_ChannelId}"" />
        </InArgument>
      </ui:LogMessage.Message>
    </ui:LogMessage>

    <!-- ── Step 2: Call Slack Integration Service – Get Channel Info ──────────────────
         IMPORTANT – Before running:
           1. Create a Slack connection in UiPath Integration Service
              (Orchestrator → Integration Service → Connections → + New Connection → Slack)
           2. Replace the ConnectionId placeholder below with the GUID of that connection.
         The workflow will fail at runtime with "invalid connection" until a real ID is provided.
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
    <isactr:ConnectorActivity
      Configuration=""
      ConnectionId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
      DisplayName="Get Channel Info (Slack)"
      UiPathActivityTypeId="f9995f55-16e3-3c65-b860-af01aa2a1e47"
      sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="ConnectorActivity_1">
      <isactr:ConnectorActivity.FieldObjects>

        <!-- INPUT: The Slack Channel ID passed in as the workflow argument -->
        <isactr:FieldObject Name="conversationsInfoId" Type="FieldArgument">
          <isactr:FieldObject.Value>
            <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
              <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="in_ChannelId" />
            </InArgument>
          </isactr:FieldObject.Value>
        </isactr:FieldObject>

        <!-- OUTPUT: The full channel record (typed JIT object at runtime; Object here as placeholder).
             In Studio with a live connection, open this activity → the designer will show the
             strongly-typed output and you can bind individual fields directly. -->
        <isactr:FieldObject Name="Jit_ConversationsInfo_GET" Type="FieldArgument">
          <isactr:FieldObject.Value>
            <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
              <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Object" ExpressionText="channelInfo" />
            </OutArgument>
          </isactr:FieldObject.Value>
        </isactr:FieldObject>

      </isactr:ConnectorActivity.FieldObjects>
    </isactr:ConnectorActivity>

    <!-- ── Step 3: Extract channel name (VB late-binding on the JIT object) ── -->
    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Extract: Channel Name" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="Assign_1">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="channelName" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String"
            ExpressionText="If(channelInfo IsNot Nothing, Convert.ToString(channelInfo.name), "")" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <!-- ── Step 4: Extract channel description (purpose.value) ── -->
    <Assign x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="Extract: Channel Description" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="Assign_2">
      <Assign.To>
        <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="channelDescription" />
        </OutArgument>
      </Assign.To>
      <Assign.Value>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String"
            ExpressionText="If(channelInfo IsNot Nothing, Convert.ToString(channelInfo.purpose.value), "(No description set)")" />
        </InArgument>
      </Assign.Value>
    </Assign>

    <!-- ── Step 5: Log the result (appears in Orchestrator / Robot log) ── -->
    <ui:LogMessage Level="Info" DisplayName="Log: Show Description" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="LogMessage_2">
      <ui:LogMessage.Message>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Object">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Object"
            ExpressionText="$"=== Slack Channel Description ==={Environment.NewLine}Channel : #{channelName}{Environment.NewLine}Description: {channelDescription}"" />
        </InArgument>
      </ui:LogMessage.Message>
    </ui:LogMessage>

    <!-- ── Step 6: Write to console (visible when running via `uip rpa run`) ── -->
    <WriteLine DisplayName="Display Result" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="WriteLine_1">
      <WriteLine.Text>
        <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
          <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String"
            ExpressionText="$"=== Slack Channel Description ==={Environment.NewLine}Channel : #{channelName}{Environment.NewLine}Description: {channelDescription}"" />
        </InArgument>
      </WriteLine.Text>
    </WriteLine>

  </Sequence>
</Activity>

## ✅ Done — Slack Channel Description workflow

**What was built:**
- **Project:** `SlackChannelDescription/` (Cross-platform, VB.NET)
- **File created/edited:** `SlackChannelDescription/Main.xaml`
- **Package installed:** `UiPath.IntegrationService.Activities` v1.29.0

**How it works:**
The automation uses UiPath's **Integration Service Slack connector** — a direct API connection, no clicking through Slack's UI. The workflow:
1. Accepts a **Channel ID** as input (`in_ChannelId`)
2. Calls Slack's `conversations.info` API via the `Get Channel Info` IS activity
3. Extracts the **channel name** and **channel description** (stored in Slack as `purpose.value`)
4. Logs the result to the robot log (visible in Orchestrator) **and** prints it to the console

**Before you can run it — one setup step:**
You need to wire up a Slack connection:
1. In Orchestrator → **Integration Service** → **Connections** → **+ New Connection** → pick **Slack** → authenticate
2. Copy the connection's **GUID**
3. Open `Main.xaml` and replace `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` (line 84) with that GUID

**How to find a channel's ID in Slack:**
Right-click the channel → *View channel details* → scroll to the bottom of the "About" tab → **Copy channel ID** (it starts with `C`, e.g. `C12345678`).

**How to run it:**
```bash
uip rpa run --file-path "Main.xaml" \
  --project-dir "./SlackChannelDescription" \
  --input-arguments '{"in_ChannelId": "C12345678"}' \
  --output json
```

**Validation status:** `validate` ✅ clean · `build` ✅ clean (`Success: true`)

If anything doesn't work as expected, use `/uipath-feedback` to send a report!

1	# Author — Create and edit `.flow` files
2	
3	Capability index for building new flows (greenfield) and editing existing flows (brownfield). Author owns everything that happens on disk, locally, without `uip login`. Authoring journeys terminate at `validate` + `format`; from there, hand off to [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md) to publish, run, or debug.
4	
5	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Author is upstream of Operate (build the flow → ship it) and upstream of Diagnose only via Operate (build → run → diagnose). Publish/run/lifecycle lives in [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md); fault triage lives in [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
6	>
7	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md)** — `--output json` + prefer `--output-filter` for extraction, no `flow debug` without consent, resource discovery order, never invoke other skills automatically, dropdown question pattern, solution layout, **plain-English narration + granular progress list (opt-in — silent by default; engage when the user asks for verbosity)**. The rules below are author-scoped and apply on top.
8	
9	## When to use this capability
10	
11	- Create a new Flow project with `uip maestro flow init`
12	- Edit a `.flow` file — adding nodes, edges, or logic
13	- Explore available node types via the registry
14	- Validate a Flow file locally
15	- Manage variables, subflows, expressions, and output wiring
16	- Apply Node ownership — who authors the node (see § below)
17	- Configure connector, connector-trigger, or managed HTTP nodes; scaffold inline-agent projects
18	- Plan a complex flow before building
19	
20	## Node ownership — who authors the node
21	
22	Every node in a `.flow` file has exactly one author. The validator enforces this.
23	
24	**User-owned nodes (Edit / Write directly):**
25	
26	| Category | Node types |
27	| --- | --- |
28	| Triggers | `core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled` |
29	| Control flow | `core.logic.decision`, `core.logic.switch`, `core.logic.loop`, `core.logic.merge`, `core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`, `core.subflow` |
30	| Logic | `core.action.script`, `core.action.transform`, `core.logic.delay`, `core.logic.mock` |
31	| Human-in-the-loop | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (inline form), `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` (app-based) |
32	| Patterns | `uipath.pattern.batch-transform`, `uipath.pattern.deep-rag` |
33	| Agents | `uipath.agent.autonomous` (inline; after `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`) |
34	| Resource nodes | `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`, `uipath.core.flow.*`, `uipath.core.agentic-process.*`, `uipath.core.api-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.human-task.*` |
35	| Queue | `core.action.queue.create`, `core.action.queue.create-and-wait` |
36	
37	**CLI-owned nodes (`uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`):**
38	
39	| Category | Node types | Why |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| Connector activities | `uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` | `inputs.detail` is a `=jsonString:essentialConfiguration` envelope. Validate rejects hand-authored shapes. |
42	| Connector triggers | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` | Same envelope + product-managed `bindings_v2.json` derivation. |
43	| Wait for events (mid-flow) | `uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>` | Same envelope and event metadata as a trigger, but placed mid-flow (has an `input` port) instead of as the start node. See [connector-trigger/impl.md — Wait for events](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent). |
44	| Managed HTTP | `core.action.http.v2` | Same envelope. |
45	
46	For CLI-owned nodes:
47	
48	- Use `uip maestro flow node add` to insert the node and copy the definition into `definitions[]`.
49	- Use `uip maestro flow node configure --detail '{...}'` to populate `inputs.detail` and `bindings[]`.
50	- Subsequent edits to `inputs.detail` are also CLI-only — re-run `node configure` (it's a full rebuild; see [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md)).
51	- You may still `Edit` the node's `display.label`, edges, layout, and outputs — those are not part of the envelope.
52	
53	If you find yourself hand-writing `inputs.detail`, a `=jsonString:` blob, or `bindings[]` entries for a connector node — stop. Use the CLI.
54	
55	## Critical rules
56	
57	1. **Always validate node types against the registry before building.** Use `registry search`/`list` for discovery and `registry get` for detailed metadata and definitions.
58	2. **ALWAYS follow the relevant plugin in [plugins/](references/plugins/) for every node type.** Each plugin has a `planning.md` (when to use, selection heuristics, ports) and `impl.md` (registry validation, JSON structure, CLI commands, configuration, debug). For connector nodes, the [connector](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) plugin covers connection binding, enriched metadata, and field resolution — required before building. Without this, node configuration will be wrong — errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
59	3. **Read the relevant Integration Service reference doc before any `uip is ...` call.** Two non-overlapping contracts:
60	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md) before any `uip is connections ...` call.** Applies to every connector activity, connector trigger, and managed HTTP node in connected mode. Single source of truth for command syntax, selection (including the personal-workspace auto-select rule), folder scoping, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, and ping verification. **If no healthy connection exists after following its recovery flow, STOP** and surface it in **Open Questions** during planning.
61	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) before any `uip is resources run ...` call.** Applies to every reference-field lookup (Slack user IDs, Jira project keys, Outlook folder IDs, etc.). Single source of truth for the `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` contract and the `--query "nextPage=<token>"` loop. **Complete the pagination loop before reporting not-found** — do NOT abandon mid-loop to try alternative endpoints, `where=` filters the connector may not support, or asking the user. Plugin files cover node-specific configuration that follows connection binding: [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), [http/impl-connector.md](references/plugins/http/impl-connector.md).
62	4. **Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` only** — other generated files (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`, `package-descriptor.json`) are managed by the CLI and may be overwritten. To declare flow inputs/outputs, add variables in the `.flow` file (see [shared/file-format.md](../shared/file-format.md)).
63	5. **`targetPort` is required on every edge** — `validate` rejects edges without it.
64	6. **Every node type needs a `definitions` entry** — copy from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type>` output. Never hand-write definitions. The definition is the sole source for BPMN type (`model.type`), serviceType, event definitions, and binding/context templates — none of that belongs on the instance.
65	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar.
66	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
67	9. **Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file** — there are no CLI commands for variable management. Use `Edit` to add/remove/update entries in the `variables` section of the `.flow` file. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
68	10. **Every `out` variable must be mapped on every reachable End node** — missing output mappings cause runtime errors. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
69	11. **`=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference in a value field** — not on condition expressions (decision, switch, HTTP branch), which are auto-evaluated as JS. Without it, the BPMN runtime sees a literal string and `flow validate` fails with MST-9107. See [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the canonical rule and per-node-type field reference, and [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the expression system.
70	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's `size` by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows (`subflows[<id>].layout`). Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.
71	13. **Don't hand-write `layout.nodes` or `subflows[<id>].layout`** — these are owned by `flow format`. When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. Sticky notes (`type: "stickyNote"`) are the one exception — format preserves their custom size and position. See [shared/file-format.md — Layout](../shared/file-format.md#layout).
72	14. **Every data-producing node MUST have a matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — this is what makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve.** The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations the runtime needs. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. See [shared/file-format.md — Node outputs](../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
73	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). The runtime hydrates these from the definition at serialization time. Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`, `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers), `color`/`content` (sticky notes), and `source` (every inline-agent-related node — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node use `inputs.source = <UUID>`; their definitions declare `model.source: true` and flow-core hoists onto the instance).

112	## Anti-patterns
113	
114	- **Prefer running `uip maestro flow init` from inside the solution you named** — run outside one it auto-scaffolds `<Project>Solution/`, but the auto name won't match your chosen solution name. Never pass `--skip-solution-registration` for a project you intend to upload (it leaves a bare single-nested layout). See [SKILL.md rule #6](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) for the required double-nested `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` layout and the self-check.
115	- **Never guess node schemas** — use `registry get` for all node types. Guessed port names or input fields cause silent wiring failures.
116	- **Never skip capability discovery for connector nodes** — run `registry search` to confirm the connector exists and what operations it supports before building. See [connector/planning.md](references/plugins/connector/planning.md). Skipping this is the #1 cause of designing around a connector that doesn't exist or an operation it doesn't support.
117	- **Never replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run** — if `registry search` / `registry get` finds `uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<operation>`, add that real connector node via `uip maestro flow node add`. Missing live connections, missing tenant access, or prompts that ask you to only plan `--detail` mean: run `node add`, write the planned `--detail` payload to a sidecar file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`), and surface "configure pending" as an Open Question. **Do not leave a partial `inputs.detail` on the node** — the validator rejects hand-authored envelopes, and the node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run. Studio Web and reviewers need the real connector key in the `.flow`; the agent must report this explicitly rather than letting the user discover it via a later validation failure. See [§ Node ownership](#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) and [connector/impl.md — No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration](references/plugins/connector/impl.md#no-live-tenant--planned-configuration).
118	- **Never edit `content/*.bpmn`** — it is auto-generated from the `.flow` file and will be overwritten.
119	- **Never use `core.logic.mock` when the resource is in the same solution** — use `--local` discovery instead. Mock placeholders are only for resources that are not in the current solution and not yet published.
120	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
121	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). Instances carry only per-instance data: `inputs`, `outputs`, `display`. Identity fields like `entryPointId` / `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers) and `color` / `content` (sticky notes) live under `inputs`. This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source = <UUID>`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance.
122	- **Never author `model.context[]` on resource-node instances** — resource-node instances have no `model` block. For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition (from `registry get`) already carries `model.context[]` with `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders. Your job is to add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two entries per resource node (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`. At BPMN emit, the runtime rewrites `<bindings.{name}>` → `=bindings.{id}` via `(resourceKey, name)` matching. Without the top-level `bindings[]` entries, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." See the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
123	- **Never put a `ui` block on node instances** — position and size belong in the top-level `layout.nodes` object. Nodes with `"ui": { "position": ... }` use the wrong format and may not render correctly in Studio Web.
124	- **Never skip `flow format` before publish or debug** — without it, hand-written `layout` data renders as misshapen rectangles in Studio Web (the MST-9061 failure mode). See rule #12 above for the format step.
125	- **Never validate after every individual edit** — intermediate flow states (e.g., node added but not yet wired) are expected to be invalid. Run `uip maestro flow validate` once after the full build is complete.
126	- **Never use `console.log` in script nodes** — `console` is not available in the Jint runtime. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
127	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
128	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
129	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.
130	- **Never use `core.action.http` (v1)** — the v1 node is deprecated for all HTTP requests (both connector-authenticated and manual). For connector-auth, v1's `authenticationType: "connection"` input does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request) for every HTTP node. See [http/planning.md](references/plugins/http/planning.md).
131	- **Never hand-write `definitions[]` or `inputs.*` for managed HTTP nodes** — use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for `branches` / `timeout` / `retryCount`) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths. Hand-written `definitions[]` strips required manifest fields; hand-written `inputs.detail` misses `essentialConfiguration` and fails at runtime. See [http/impl.md](references/plugins/http/impl.md).
132	- **Never write `$vars.X` (or `$metadata.X`, `$self.X`) without `=js:` in value fields** — `flow validate` flags this as MST-9107. See rule #11 above and [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-node-type field reference.
133	- **Never reuse a reference ID (mailbox folder, Slack channel, Jira project, Google Sheet, etc.) from a prior flow or session** — reference IDs are scoped to the specific authenticated account behind the connection. A `parentFolderId` from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another; a Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A reused ID passes `flow validate` and `node configure` cleanly, then faults silently at runtime with no resolvable error. Always re-resolve via `uip is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID> --output json` against the connection bound to this flow — do not paste a value you saw in another flow. See [connector/impl.md — Step 4](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) and [connector-trigger/impl.md — Step 3](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md).
134	- **Never include `[*]` literally in a connector `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key** — `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` is an array marker, not part of the wire key. Strip it and pass an array value of the field's `dataType` (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": ["a", "b"]`). Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix; `[*].` (segments after) is not authorable. `flow validate` misses this; runtime rejects the key. See [connector/impl.md — Step 6b](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the full table including expression-value handling.

1	# Greenfield — Create a New Flow
2	
3	End-to-end journey for creating a Flow project from scratch. Author terminates at `validate` + `format`. To publish, run, or debug after this, see [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md).
4	
5	> **Brownfield edits use a different journey.** If the `.flow` file already exists, see [brownfield.md](brownfield.md) instead.
6	
7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10	
11	**Plan when:**
12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach
15	
16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)
19	- The user has already described the exact topology they want
20	
21	### Examples
22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."
24	→ Multiple services, branching logic, connector discovery needed. Plan first.
25	
26	**Don't plan:** "Create a flow that calls an API and sends the result to Slack."
27	→ Linear pipeline, user knows what they want. Build directly, ask questions inline if needed. **"Build directly" skips the plan doc, not the registry search** — you still `registry search` each named service and pick a node type via the Step 3 ladder.
28	
29	**Judgment call:** "Build me a flow that processes invoices."
30	→ Ambiguous requirements. Ask clarifying questions; plan if answers reveal complexity.
31	
32	## Three-turn execution map
33	
34	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
35	
36	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s) **+** optional `uip login status`. **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
39	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
40	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
41	
42	### Batching anti-patterns
43	
44	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
45	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
46	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
47	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
48	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
49	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.
50	
51	## Step 0 — Resolve the `uip` binary and detect command prefix **[T1]**
52	
53	See [shared/cli-conventions.md](../../shared/cli-conventions.md) for binary resolution, version detection, and the `uip maestro flow` vs `uip flow` command prefix rule. All commands below are written in the `uip maestro flow` form. <!-- uip-check-skip -->
54	
55	This probe is read-only — emit as a parallel `Bash` alongside the Step 2 scaffold chain. It does not need its own turn.

57	## Step 1 — Check login status **[T1 — only if needed]**
58	
59	Greenfield steps 2–6 work without login (`flow init`, `validate`, `format`, registry OOTB nodes, `Edit` / `Write` edits). Login is required only when the registry needs tenant-specific connector/resource nodes, or before handing off to Operate.
60	
61	```bash
62	uip login status --output json
63	```
64	
65	If not logged in and you need tenant nodes:
66	
67	```bash
68	uip login                                          # interactive OAuth (opens browser)
69	uip login --authority https://alpha.uipath.com     # non-production environments
70	```
71	
72	When you do need it, emit `uip login status --output json` as a parallel `Bash` inside T1.

74	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
75	
76	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so the solution name matches the project name rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
77	
78	Check for existing solutions with `ls *.uipx */*.uipx 2>/dev/null` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask via `AskUserQuestion`, presenting a dropdown with one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** as the last option. The user wanting a new solution does not let you skip this; you only learn that by asking. If none are found, create a new one automatically. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md).
79	
80	- If the user specifies an existing `.uipx` file path or solution name, use that (skip to Step 2b)
81	- Otherwise, create a new solution (Step 2a)
82	
83	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
84	
85	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
86	
87	```bash
88	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
89	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
90	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
91	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
92	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
93	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
94	```
95	
96	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
97	
98	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
99	
100	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.
101	
102	The sub-steps below describe what each command in the chain does and how to verify the result.
103	
104	### 2a. Create a new solution
105	
106	```bash
107	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
108	```
109	
110	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
111	
112	> **Naming convention:** Use the same name for both the solution and the project unless the user specifies otherwise. If the user only provides a project name, use it as the solution name too.
113	
114	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
115	
116	```bash
117	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
118	```
119	
120	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
121	
122	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.
123	
124	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.
125	
126	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
127	
128	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:
129	
130	```json
131	{
132	  "Result": "Success",
133	  "Code": "FlowInit",
134	  "Data": {
135	    "Status": "Created successfully",
136	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
137	    "SolutionRegistration": {
138	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
139	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
140	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
141	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
142	    }
143	  }
144	}
145	```
146	
147	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.
148	
149	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.
150	
151	```bash
152	uip solution project add \
153	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<ProjectName> \
154	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx
155	```
156	
157	If you ended up with a bare single-nested layout (e.g. `--skip-solution-registration` was passed), **delete the partial scaffold and restart from Step 2a** — do not try to patch the layout by hand. See [diagnose/references/failure-modes.md — Single-nested layout](../../diagnose/references/failure-modes.md#single-nested-layout).
158	
159	### Expected layout after Steps 2a–2c
160	
161	```
162	<cwd>/
163	└── <SolutionName>/                    ← from `uip solution init`
164	    ├── <SolutionName>.uipx
165	    └── <ProjectName>/                 ← from `uip maestro flow init` (run from inside <SolutionName>/)
166	        ├── <ProjectName>.flow         ← the file you edit
167	        ├── project.uiproj
168	        ├── bindings_v2.json
169	        ├── entry-points.json
170	        ├── operate.json
171	        └── package-descriptor.json
172	```
173	
174	**Self-check — run this before Step 3:**
175	
176	After Step 2b your cwd is inside `<SolutionName>/` (the `cd` persists). Verify the flow file using a `$(pwd)`-anchored absolute path so the check is robust to that cwd drift:
177	
178	```bash
179	ls "$(pwd)/<ProjectName>/<ProjectName>.flow"
180	```
181	
182	Equivalent: use the absolute project dir reported by `flow init` in `Data.Path` and append `/<ProjectName>.flow`. Either form gives an absolute path that doesn't depend on the current cwd.
183	
184	> **Don't write `<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>/<ProjectName>.flow` here.** From inside `<SolutionName>/` that resolves to `<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>/<ProjectName>.flow` (triple-nested) and the `ls` will fail even though the layout is correct. That false negative wastes turns chasing a non-bug.
185	
186	If the file does not exist at the absolute double-nested path, Step 2 is wrong. Delete the partial scaffold and restart from Step 2a — do not try to patch the layout by hand.
187	
188	See [shared/file-format.md](../../shared/file-format.md) for the full project structure.

190	## Step 3 — Refresh the registry **[T1 — chained tail of Step 2]**
191	
192	This is already the last segment of the [canonical T1 chain](#canonical-t1-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. Standalone:
193	
194	```bash
195	uip maestro flow registry pull                          # refresh local cache (expires after 30 min)
196	```
197	
198	**Parallel `registry get`** — in the same T1 assistant message, emit one separate `Bash` per OOTB node type whose definition you'll inline in T2. **Always fetch `core.control.end`** — `flow init` does not scaffold one (see Step 4):
199	
200	```bash
201	uip maestro flow registry get core.control.end --output json
202	```

204	> **Auth note**: Without `uip login`, registry shows OOTB nodes only. After login, tenant-specific connector and resource nodes are also available. **In-solution sibling projects** are always available via `--local` without login — see below.

206	### Select the node type for each external service (runs even when full planning is skipped)
207	
208	Calling a named external service (Slack, open-meteo, Stripe, any REST API)? **Search first — never guess the node type from the brand name:**
209	
210	```bash
211	uip maestro flow registry search "<service>" --output json --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
212	```

214	Then pick the first match down this ladder:
215	
216	1. **Curated connector activity** (`uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` in the results) → use it.
217	2. **Connector exists but no activity for what you need** → `core.action.http.v2` (connector mode).
218	3. **No connector at all** → `core.action.http.v2` (manual mode).
219	4. **No API** (desktop app) → [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
220	
221	Manual HTTP is the **bottom of the ladder** — only the search returning no connector authorizes it. Picking it without searching is the brand-name shortcut forbidden by [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal).
222	
223	**In-solution discovery (no login required):**
224	
225	```bash
226	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json     # discover sibling projects in the same .uipx solution
227	uip maestro flow registry search "<keyword>" --local --output json  # keyword search across in-solution nodes
228	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json  # get full manifest for a local node
229	```
230	
231	Run from inside the flow project directory. Returns the same manifest format as the tenant registry. Use `--local` to wire in-solution resources (RPA, agents, flows, API workflows) without publishing them first. `search --local` omits `AvailableOnTenant` — drop it from `--output-filter` projections.
